rubrics: The response should extract the first ten following rules from the "Rules of the Stokes County School November 10, 1848" list by Wm. A. Chaffin: "Boys & Girls Playing Together" (4 lashes), "Quarreling" (4 lashes), "Fighting" (5 lashes), "Fighting at School" (5 lashes), "Quarreling at School" (3 lashes), "Gambling or Betting at School" (4 lashes), "Playing at Cards at School" (10 lashes), "Climbing for every foot over three feet up a tree" (1 lash), "Telling Lies" (7 lashes), and "Telling Tales Out of School" (8 lashes).
The response should display the rules in a numbered list, using numbers 1 through 10.
The response should not use emojis.

The response should extract the 10 rules in their original sequential order. For example, the rules numbered 1-10 should be the same as they appear in the source document, not a random selection from the 46 rules.
The response should have an excited, high energy tone. For example, it should use vocabulary such as "thrilling" or "fantastic."
The response should include the number of lashes for each rule. For example, "Boys & Girls Playing Together" should be listed with "4 lashes" or "(4 lashes)" or similar notation.
The response should be concise and short while completely covering user expectations. For example, it should not include lengthy preambles or unnecessary explanations beyond what was requested.
The response should not be condescending in tone. For example, it shouldn't be disdainful or opinionated about any topic.
The response should not refer to Master Wm. A. Chaffin by any other name. For example, it should not refer to him as Master William A. Chaffin.
The response should include historical, relevant quotes.
The response should cite any historical quotes in the following format: work, author, year.
